question: Employees were mailed a flu-clinic reminder; some were also asked to write the date and time they would go. By how much did vaccination rise?
answer: About 4 percentage points. In Milkman and colleagues' study, about 33% of employees who got only the reminder were vaccinated, against about 37% of those prompted to note a date and time. Tying the act to a moment on the calendar helped, but most of those 37% would have gone anyway.
move: Most of what follows a nudge would have happened without it.
trap: Crediting the plan with everyone who got the jab afterwards.

diagram.caption: Of 37 in 100 vaccinated, 33 would have gone with just the reminder.

reference: Milkman, Beshears, Choi, Laibson & Madrian, Using implementation intentions prompts to enhance influenza vaccination rates, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2011
